sentences.text: Austroptyctodus gardineri was a small placoderm fish, an armored ancestor of modern bony fish, belonging to the ptyctodontid group. Unlike many relatives, this genus lacked spinal plates but possessed toothplates similar to those of Ptyctodus.
A fossil specimen shows a female pregnant with three embryos, proving the genus was a live-bearer that reproduced via internal fertilization.

The species was first described in 1977 by Miles and Young as a new species of the genus Ctenurella. In 1997, Long redescribed the material and established the new genus Austroptyctodus based on differences in the skull roof pattern.

Fossil evidence of ostracods found in the abdominal region indicates the fish consumed these small crustaceans. The presence of nocturnal ostracods in its stomach suggests Austroptyctodus was a nocturnal hunter.
Ctenurella gardineri is a synonym for Austroptyctodus gardineri. Austroptyctodus is classified within the parent group Placodermi.

The fossil range of Austroptyctodus extends into the Late Frasnian stage. The species lived during the Upper Devonian period in the Gogo Formation of Western Australia. The genus lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
